subject.title: [Bug] gateway shutdown timed out: node report shows active child process handle; leaves dirty shutdown + lane wait

question: On normal gateway stop or SIGTERM, should OpenClaw terminate active supervised exec child processes, preserve background exec work, or add a narrower opt-in/diagnostic shutdown policy?
rationale: Current source makes both sides real: dirty shutdowns are a production reliability bug, but existing tests and comments intentionally preserve active/background work on normal stop, so automation should not choose cancellation semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Bound foreground cancellation
options.body: Cancel non-background supervised exec work during normal shutdown, preserve explicit background sessions unless separately killed, and emit diagnostics for any remaining child handles.

options.title: Kill all supervised exec
options.body: Treat gateway stop as an operator-owned hard boundary and terminate all supervised child process trees before the watchdog fires, accepting the upgrade behavior change.

options.title: Preserve current default
options.body: Keep normal stop non-destructive and improve diagnostics or operator commands, accepting that long-running children may still force dirty shutdown until manually handled.

recommendation.title: Bound foreground cancellation
recommendation.body: Cancel non-background supervised exec work during normal shutdown, preserve explicit background sessions unless separately killed, and emit diagnostics for any remaining child handles.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest combined signal across recent gateway close, exec behavior, and prior review routing for the shutdown-policy decision.
